question: Where can I get the capacity of the gas grid to receive biomethane injection in Spain, by zone or connection point?

answer.summary: No single national registry publishes biomethane injection capacity by zone or connection point in Spain. Under CNMC Circular 2/2025 (Art. 40), operators must publish capacity by network segment, but only Gas Extremadura publishes granted and in-process injection capacity plus flow percentiles (2023-2025 PDFs for Extremadura). Major DSOs (Nortegas, Nedgia, Redexis, Madrileña Red de Gas) only publish >=16 bar schematics and historical demand/flow proxies, while Enagás Transporte requires registration on ServiceNow; remaining gaps require prior-information requests to each operator.
main_caveats: Despite Circular 2/2025 Art. 40.3 mandating capacity by segment, 4 of 5 major DSOs tested (Nortegas, Nedgia, Redexis, Madrileña) only publish >=16 bar schematics and historical demand/flows, omitting granted or free injection capacity.

Historical gas demand/flows act only as an upper-bound proxy: already-granted or queued injections, downstream sensitive consumers, and reverse-flow limits can reduce or block actual injection capacity.
Enagás Transporte (national primary transmission grid, P > 60 bar) places network schemes, historical consumptions, and biomethane pre-requests behind mandatory company registration on ServiceNow.

Enagás GTS publishes conditional capacity by area ONLY for hydrogen (a gas requiring mixing, Circular 2/2025 Art. 40.2); biomethane does not require mixing and is governed per operator under Art. 40.3.

Published data live in unstandardized PDFs without machine-readable coordinates; Gas Extremadura omits an explicit unit label on its granted and in-process columns (implicitly Nm3/h matching flow rows).
answer.confidence_reason: Directly verified BOE Circular 2/2025 & Res. 13/06/2025, CNMC census/reports, MITECO, Enagás GTS/Transporte, all 5 major DSO portals with downloaded PDFs, 4 minor DSOs, and non-official maps in this session.

local_terms.meaning: Conditional firm connection/access capacity granted to renewable gas plants subject to predefined flow, demand, and gas-quality conditions.
Legal category in Circular 2/2025 for injectable non-fossil gases; split into gases not needing mixing (biomethane) and gases needing mixing (hydrogen).
Reverse flow from a distribution/secondary grid upstream into transmission when biomethane supply exceeds local downstream demand.
Connection points between transmission-transmission (PCTT), transmission-distribution (PCTD), and distribution-distribution (PCDD) networks.
Connection point for biomethane/renewable gas injection into a transmission pipeline (punto de conexión para inyección en gasoducto de transporte).
Spanish gas grid tiers under Law 34/1998: >=60 bar (primary transmission), 16-60 bar (secondary transmission), and <=16 bar (distribution).
Formal pre-application inquiry (Res. 13/06/2025 Apartado Cuarto) requiring network owners to reply within 1 month with UTM points, P5/P95 flows, and granted/queued capacity.
Sistema Logístico de Acceso de Terceros, the Enagás GTS platform where commissioned biomethane injection points are registered for PVB market access.
